title: configASSERT in vPortValidateInterruptPriority
serial_logs:
[boot] scheduler started
ASSERT FAILED: port.c vPortValidateInterruptPriority
  ucCurrentPriority=0x00 ucMaxSysCallPriority=0x50
System halted.
user_question: Crashes on the first byte received.

reference_context.title: FreeRTOS Kernel Documentation (freertos.org)
reference_context.document: FreeRTOS: Running the RTOS on a ARM Cortex-M Core
reference_context.section: Inverse Relationship Between Numeric Priority Value and the Logical Priority Setting > Relevance when using the RTOS
reference_context.snippet: Therefore, any interrupt service routine that uses an RTOS API function must have its priority manually set to a value that is numerically equal to or greater than the configMAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY setting. This ensures the interrupt's logical priority is equal to or less than the configMAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY setting. Cortex-M interrupts default to having a priority value of zero.

expected.root_cause: USART2_IRQn is set to NVIC priority 0, which is above configMAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY (5), yet its ISR calls xQueueSendFromISR, tripping the configASSERT.
expected.fix: Set the USART2 priority to 5 or higher numerically, e.g. HAL_NVIC_SetPriority(USART2_IRQn, 5, 0).
